html:
A series of huge waves set off by an undersea earthquake of magnitude about 9.2 off northern Sumatra on 26 December 2004. It killed about 230,000 people in fourteen countries, one of the deadliest natural disasters in history.

The quake struck off Aceh, which suffered worst. Within two hours the waves crossed the Bay of Bengal. In Sri Lanka some 35,000 people died; a train full of passengers was swept away near Peraliya, the worst rail disaster ever. In India over ten thousand died, mainly in Tamil Nadu and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. In the Maldives, low islands were swamped, though deaths were fewer. The waves even reached East Africa.

There was no warning system in the Indian Ocean, and most people had no idea that a sea drawing back meant danger. Afterwards countries built one, in place from 2006. Aid poured in on a vast scale. In Aceh, the disaster helped bring a peace deal between rebels and the government in 2005; in Sri Lanka, quarrels over aid deepened the civil war. In Galle, the old walls of Galle Fort held back the sea.
sum: A series of huge waves set off by an undersea earthquake of magnitude about 9.2 off northern Sumatra on 26 December 2004. It killed about 230,000 people in fourteen countries, one of the deadliest natural disasters in history.
